subject: MSA negotiation — liability categories, caps, and carve-outs
messages:
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Elaine Johnson <elaine.johnson@acme.com>, counsel@mgllaw.com
Date: 2026-06-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MSA redlines — liability / indirect damages

Laura — attaching Acme's redline of the MSA (see attachment). High level: Acme can't accept broad exclusion of consequential damages for the categories that matter to our business (lost profits, reputational harm, loss of data). We're proposing: a carve-out for IP infringement and data loss (unlimited for indemnity/repair costs), and a waiver of consequential-damages exclusion for lost profits caused by Redwood's gross negligence.

Key asks in the redline: 
- Remove blanket exclusion for lost profits.
- Unlimited liability for IP infringement and first-party data loss remediation.
- Cap on non-excluded liability: 24 months of fees or $10M (whichever is greater).

We also included examples to show the impact (downtime during peak quarter = ~ $1.2M estimated lost revenue). Please review and let us know Redwood's position.

[attachment: MSA_Redline_v3.docx]

Thanks,
Tom
Director, Procurement
Acme Corporation

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme.com>, Elaine Johnson <elaine.johnson@acme.com>, counsel@mgllaw.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-21T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: MSA redlines — liability / indirect damages

Tom / Elaine — thanks for the redline and the examples, they're helpful. A few principles from our side:

1) Predictable unit economics: we need a commercially reasonable aggregate cap to manage risk across our hosted customers.
2) Carve-outs: we are open to carve-outs for liability tied to our willful misconduct and for third-party IP infringement where our indemnity applies, but unlimited liability is not acceptable.
3) Direct vs indirect: we want clear drafting that preserves "direct damages" (costs to remediate, reasonable third-party costs) while excluding consequential categories (lost profits, loss of goodwill) except in limited circumstances.

Proposed compromise (high level):
- Aggregate cap: lesser of $5,000,000 or 12 months of fees paid under the applicable Order Form.
- Carve-outs from cap: (i) liability arising from Redwood's willful misconduct or gross negligence; (ii) Redwood's indemnity for IP infringement (subject to mitigation and control provisions) — but indemnity recoveries limited to amounts awarded in a final judgment or settlement; (iii) amounts payable under confidentiality breach obligations for personally identifiable data remediation (capped at fees).
- Consequential damages: exclude consequential/indirect damages (including lost profits, loss of business, loss of goodwill), but specifically allow recoverable direct costs to restore customer data or reasonable incremental costs incurred to operate during downtime.

I'll follow up with markups of the specific clauses this afternoon. If you have internal examples of acceptable cap math (e.g., how you get to 24 months / $10M), share them and we can see if there's a middle path.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference

From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Elaine Johnson <elaine.johnson@acme.com>, counsel@mgllaw.com
Date: 2026-06-22T08:46:00-07:00
Subject: RE: MSA redlines — liability / indirect damages

Rishi — thanks. A couple quick clarifications from Acme's side:

1) IP infringement: Acme's concern is real-world risk — an infringement claim can threaten our product and business continuity. We need indemnity that covers remediation costs, regulatory fines, and lost profits arising from the infringement. Unlimited makes sense for indemnity tied to IP; otherwise the cap doesn't provide protection.

2) Data loss: if customer data is lost or corrupted due to Redwood's error, recovery costs (forensics, restoration, customer notifications, regulatory fines) can be well in excess of fees. We asked for unlimited (or at least a much higher cap) here.

3) Lost profits: we're asking for lost profits where there's a direct causal link to an outage caused by Redwood's failure to meet SLOs. We can live with a higher cap if there's objective metric-based carve-out tied to SLO breaches, but blanket exclusion is unacceptable.

We want to avoid lengthy back-and-forth. If you can provide sample clause language that (a) preserves a measurable right to lost profits in SLO breach scenarios and (b) limits exposure elsewhere, we can take that back to procurement.

Tom

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Team — looping you both in so we can coordinate a response and a drafting playbook. Action items: 

- Rishi: can you prepare two short drafting options (1: conservative legal position we can defend; 2: commercial compromise we can offer to close) that explicitly separate "direct damages" (data restoration, reasonable third-party costs) from "consequential" (lost profits, loss of goodwill)? Please include a narrowly tailored SLO-triggered lost-profits carve-out (example: if Redwood misses monthly uptime SLA by >2% resulting in an outage >6 hours during customer-defined peak window).
- Marissa: please confirm commercial parameters you can accept (cap levels, months-of-fees multipliers) and whether we can offer a temporary trial uplift for strategic accounts.
- Priya: please pull the Redwood_Liability_Playbook and any past redlines for similar enterprise deals we offered in last 12 months.

I'll need a one-page summary and sample clause language by EOD 7/8 so we can push the updated redline to Acme. Attaching our internal playbook for reference.

[attachment: Redwood_Liability_Playbook.pdf]

Thanks,
Laura

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme.com>, Elaine Johnson <elaine.johnson@acme.com>, counsel@mgllaw.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-08T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: MSA negotiation — liability categories, caps, and carve-outs (proposed compromise)

Tom / Elaine — thanks for the patience. Per Laura's note and our internal review, attached is a proposed compromise redline (MSA_Redline_v4.docx). High-level summary and concrete drafting we propose: 

1) Aggregate cap (compromise): Redwood's aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement will not exceed the lesser of (a) USD 5,000,000 and (b) the Fees paid by Customer to Redwood under the applicable Order Form in the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to liability.

2) Carve-outs from cap: the foregoing cap will not apply to (a) liabilities arising from Redwood's willful misconduct or gross negligence; (b) Redwood's indemnity obligations for third-party claims of intellectual property infringement, provided that Customer (i) promptly notifies Redwood, (ii) allows Redwood to control the defense and settlement, and (iii) mitigates damages; and (c) statutory obligations for data breach notification and regulatory fines (subject to limitation to amounts reasonably incurred and proof of causation). Note: for (b) indemnity recoveries, recoverable amounts are limited to amounts finally awarded by a court or paid in settlement.

3) Consequential/indirect damages: Except for the carve-outs above, neither party will be liable for consequential, special, indirect, incidental, or punitive damages, including lost profits, loss of business, and loss of goodwill.

4) Direct-data-recovery carve-out (narrow): Costs reasonably and actually incurred by Customer to restore or recover Customer Data caused by Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct are recoverable as direct damages, but such recovery will be subject to a sub-cap equal to the lesser of (a) the aggregate cap above and (b) the Fees paid in the 6 months prior to the event. This is intended to cover forensic recovery, reasonable third-party restoration costs, and documented remediation expenses.

5) SLO-triggered lost-profits (limited exception): Where Redwood fails to meet a Customer-specific SLO set forth in an Order Form (for example: monthly uptime less than X% resulting in an outage > Y hours during a Customer-defined peak window), Customer may recover proven lost profit damages directly attributable to that outage, subject to a further sub-cap equal to 3x the monthly recurring fees for the impacted service for the month in which the outage occurred, and only upon demonstration of direct causation. This is a narrowly tailored mechanism to address Acme's SLO concern without opening a broad lost-profits exposure.

6) Mitigation and proof: Any recovery for direct or SLO-triggered lost profits requires (a) customer reasonable mitigation steps, (b) contemporaneous evidence (SLO logs, incident timelines), and (c) prompt notice to Redwood.

Drafting examples included in attachment (excerpted here):
- "Direct Damages" defined as: "reasonable, documented costs to repair or restore Customer Data, and reasonable third-party costs paid to restore services; excludes lost profits, loss of business, and other consequential losses except as expressly provided in Section X (SLO-triggered lost profits)."
- SLO-trigger clause example: "If Redwood fails to meet the Uptime SLO set forth in Order Form Exhibit A for two (2) consecutive months and such failure results in an outage exceeding six (6) hours during a Customer-identified peak window, Customer may recover direct lost profits up to an amount equal to three (3) times the Monthly Recurring Fees for the impacted Services for the month in which the outage occurred, subject to demonstration of direct causation and mitigation."

Rationale: this structure keeps our aggregate exposure predictable, preserves indemnity control and defense rights, and gives Acme a measurable pathway to recover meaningful direct losses tied to major SLO failures or data loss events.

If Acme can accept this, we'll convert the language into tracked changes in the redline and send back. If you want a higher cap, Marissa, note the commercial trade (e.g., 24 months of fees or $10M requires C-level approval and will likely need additional commercial uplift).

[attachment: MSA_Redline_v4.docx]

Next steps: Please confirm whether Acme wants the tracked-changes doc or a clean copy and whether they will loop procurement for expedited sign-off. Happy to hop on a call this week to walk through the SLO-trigger math.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
